title: Spot inappropriate α and AVE on a formative construct
skills: Matching quality criteria to the measurement model

brief.text: The retail model (SYNTHETIC) has a composite-formative convenience index F (f1–f4) and reflective constructs X and Y. A reviewer writes:
"The authors do not report Cronbach's α and AVE for F. I computed them myself: α = .52 and AVE = .41, both below accepted thresholds. Please drop the weakest indicators of F until α exceeds .70."
brief.title: Reviewer 2

brief.text: Run the model and prepare a methodologically sound response.

tasks.prompt: How should you respond to the reviewer?

options.text: Explain that α and AVE assume a common factor and are not meaningful for a formative index; report weights with intervals, loadings, indicator VIFs and the content definition instead.
options.feedback: Correct. The criteria must match the measurement model (Hair et al. 2022; Cenfetelli & Bassellier 2009).

options.text: Drop f3 and f4 as requested, since α then rises.
options.feedback: Deleting components of an index changes its meaning, and α is not a criterion it must meet.

options.text: Re-specify F as reflective so that α and AVE can be reported.
options.feedback: The specification follows from the construct definition, not from the criteria a reviewer asks for.

tasks.prompt: Which results do you report for F? Select all that apply.

options.text: Outer weights with bootstrap confidence intervals

options.feedback: Correct. They help decide about indicators with small weights.
Correct. Mode B weights are sensitive to collinearity.
HTMT assumes reflective measurement; SEM Lab does not compute it for composite-formative blocks.
Like α, ρC is a common-factor reliability.

tasks.prompt: Read the indicator VIFs of F. What do they show?

options.text: All are about 1.1–1.2, so collinearity does not threaten the weights.
options.feedback: Correct. Well below the heuristic limits of 3 and 5.

options.text: They are high, so F should be reflective.
options.feedback: They are low; and VIF never decides the measurement model.

options.text: They cannot be computed for formative constructs.
options.feedback: Indicator VIFs are precisely a formative-construct diagnostic.

tasks.prompt: Enter the outer loading of f1 (with F composite-formative).
tasks.feedbackCorrect: Correct. f1 also has a sizeable absolute contribution.
tasks.feedbackWrong: Not the expected value. Make sure F is composite-formative and that you read the loading, not the weight.

hints: What does α assume about the relation between the indicators?
Would you expect opening hours and parking to correlate strongly? Should they?
The Results page marks some criteria as not applicable for F. Which ones, and why?

solution.text: α (.52) and AVE (.41) come from treating F as reflective; for a formative index they are not meaningful, and deleting components to raise α would change what F measures. Report F's weights with bootstrap intervals, its loadings (f1 ≈ .655), its indicator VIFs (all ≈ 1.1–1.2) and the content definition; a redundancy analysis against a global convenience item would add convergent-validity evidence.
